newsitem.title: USA: MSRB's Taylor attacks lawyer's remarks on SEC case.
newsitem.headline: MSRB's Taylor attacks lawyer's remarks on SEC case.

text.p: MSRB's top staff member lashed out late Monday at bond lawyers who think the SEC went too far in bringing securities fraud charges against an Arizona county over disclosure in two 1993 municipal bond issues.
Securities and Exchange Commission on Sept 30 charged Maricopa County with securities fraud and instituted cease and desist proceedings against the county.
SEC said the county failed to disclose current information about the county's worsening fiscal condition in bond documents for the July 1993 offerings.

Christopher Taylor, executive director of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, told bond analysts meeting here this week, "I was shocked and stunned to read that a bond lawyer (suggested) you really didn't have to worry about disclosure (on GO bond deals) because the issuer had the ability to levy taxes sufficient to pay debt service."

Tayor was referring to a statement by Fredric Weber, a bond lawyer with Fulbright & Jaworsky in Houston, who told The Bond Buyer this week that Maricopa County's budget deficits and use of proceeds for cash flow purposes may not have been material to investors.
Taylor said, "For people to suggest in 1996 that the industry does not need information, goes against everything that has gone before and ignores the existence of the securities laws."

He pointed to statements by local New York City officials, just before the city's 1975 fiscal crisis, who claimed the city's bonds have strong credit quality. "That all went down the chute," Taylor said.

Referring to Weber's reported remark, Taylor said, "That kind of remark invites critics of this industry, which has made tremendous progress in a relatively short period of time to get more information out there."
